stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\sqrt[3]{27x^{4}y^{-2}}\cdot\left(9x^{2}y\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$, where $x>0$ and $y>0$?
stimulus: A printmaker models how evenly ink spreads across an etched plate using two positive quantities: $x$, the depth of the etched lines, and $y$, the pressure of the press.
explanation: Write each factor with fractional exponents, and apply the exponent to the coefficient as well as to the variables. $\sqrt[3]{27x^{4}y^{-2}}=3x^{4/3}y^{-2/3}$ and $\left(9x^{2}y\right)^{-1/2}=\tfrac{1}{3}x^{-1}y^{-1/2}$. When you multiply, the coefficients cancel ($3\cdot\tfrac13=1$) and you add the exponents: $x^{4/3-1}=x^{1/3}$ and $y^{-2/3-1/2}=y^{-7/6}$. Over a denominator of 6 this is $\dfrac{x^{2/6}}{y^{7/6}}=\sqrt[6]{\dfrac{x^{2}}{y^{7}}}$. Check with $x=2$, $y=3$: both the original and this choice come to about $0.350$.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. You took the cube root of the variables but left the 27 as it was, then multiplied it by $9^{-1/2}=\tfrac13$ and got 9. The cube root applies to 27 as well, which gives 3, so the coefficients cancel to 1.

B.why: You converted everything correctly but lost a sign when you combined the powers of $y$. You worked out $-\tfrac23+\tfrac12=-\tfrac16$, but the second exponent is $-\tfrac12$, so the sum is $-\tfrac23-\tfrac12=-\tfrac76$.

D.why: You multiplied the exponents of matching bases when you should have added them. For $x$ you did $\tfrac43\cdot(-1)=-\tfrac43$, and for $y$ you did $(-\tfrac23)(-\tfrac12)=\tfrac13$. When you multiply two powers of the same base, you add the exponents.

stem:
Which of the following expressions are equivalent to the given expression?

I. $\sqrt[12]{2^{n}}$
II. $\sqrt[24]{4^{n}}$
III. $\dfrac{\sqrt[4]{2^{n}}}{\sqrt[3]{2^{n}}}$
stimulus: A musicologist studying twelve-tone equal temperament writes the frequency ratio between two pitches that are $n$ semitones apart as $\dfrac{\left(\sqrt[4]{8}\right)^{n}}{\sqrt[3]{4^{n}}}$, where $n$ is a positive integer.
explanation: Rewrite everything as a power of 2. $\left(\sqrt[4]{8}\right)^{n}=\left(2^{3}\right)^{n/4}=2^{3n/4}$ and $\sqrt[3]{4^{n}}=\left(2^{2}\right)^{n/3}=2^{2n/3}$, so the ratio is $2^{3n/4-2n/3}=2^{n/12}$. I: $\sqrt[12]{2^{n}}=2^{n/12}$, so it is equivalent. II: $\sqrt[24]{4^{n}}=\left(2^{2}\right)^{n/24}=2^{n/12}$, so it is equivalent. III: $2^{n/4}\div2^{n/3}=2^{n/4-n/3}=2^{-n/12}$, which is the reciprocal and not equal for any positive $n$. So only I and II are equivalent.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. You confirmed statement I and stopped, or you rejected II because its base is 4 and you did not rewrite $4^{n}$ as $2^{2n}$. Once you do, II is $2^{2n/24}=2^{n/12}$, so it is also equivalent.

C.why: You rejected II because you did not rewrite base 4 as $2^{2}$. You also accepted III because you subtracted its exponents in the wrong order and got $\tfrac13-\tfrac14=\tfrac1{12}$. The quotient is $2^{n/4-n/3}$, which gives a negative exponent, so III is the reciprocal of the ratio.

D.why: You handled I and II correctly, but in III you subtracted the exponents in the wrong order. The numerator's exponent $\tfrac{n}{4}$ is smaller than the denominator's $\tfrac{n}{3}$, so III equals $2^{-n/12}$, not $2^{n/12}$.
